We have won the 1953 election. A new chapter begins for Sordland.
Electoral Campaign Finance Bill
Campaign Finance Bill

Section I of this bill stipulates a significant change in the methodology of public funds allocation to political parties. The new measure replaces the previous system, based on the number of votes won in the general election, with a system reliant on the proportion of seats secured by a political party in the Assembly.

Section II sets the annual financial allocation to political parties at 500,000 Ren per each Member of Assembly. This shift ensures that financial support from public funds aligns more closely with a party's representative influence within the legislative body.

Section III, a consequential effect of these amendments, will effectively lead to a substantial increase in the election budget for the USP and a minor augmentation for other parties present in the Assembly. This restructuring of funding fosters a more proportional representation of party presence within the Assembly.

Section IV highlights an important consequence of this reallocation. Parties that do not meet the 10% election threshold will see their public funding effectively curtailed. This measure ensures that public resources are concentrated towards parties with a significant representation in the Assembly.
The CFB bill has been passed by the GNA.
Congratulations from PM Van Hoorten

Prime Minister Van Hoorten congratulated us on our election and praised our party’s stance on just and transparent elections. He signalled his wishes to continue the trade partnership between our countries as equal partners, as opposed to earlier trade deals which he believes gave Sordland unfair advantages.
Lack of Investment

The mayor of Arvory, Eric Niel, reports a lack of adequate infrastructure around Arvory which seriously undermines the attractiveness of Arvory’s investment climate. Foreign investors, particularly from Agnolia, are becoming hesitant to invest in the city.

Meanwhile, according to data published by the National Business Council, around 19 percent of a company's total expenditures in Agnland is absorbed by logistics costs, while in peer regions this figure is below ten percent.
ATO Advocates for Global Human Rights Amid Tensions

In response to growing global tensions, the Arcasian Treaty Organisation, an intergovernmental military and economic alliance of 14 countries led primarily by Arcasia, has issued an expansive report examining the state of human rights worldwide. Amid intensifying nuclear developments and efforts to counteract the expanding influence of the Contanan Security Pact, the ATO's commitment to championing human rights remains unwavering.

The report meticulously identifies regions worldwide where human rights are most endangered, shedding light on areas of concern in multiple continents, including eastern Merkopa, western Rika, and southern Contana. Proposed strategies underline the need for actionable, collaborative efforts to address these crises, championing an international focus on basic human rights and freedom. 

As the specter of potential tensions and proxy wars looms, the report calls for nations to remember that the fight for universal respect for human dignity transcends political and ideological divisions.
Booming Wine Demand in Borin

In Borin, there has been a significant surge in demand for local wines. This sudden increase has led to a busy season for vineyards and wineries across the region. The cause of this rise in demand comes from international interest, and it is certainly driving economic activity in the city. Wineries are ramping up production to meet the increased demand. 

A continued trend could further stimulate the region's economy.
CSP and Federation of Anraka Sign Historic NAP

A significant step forward in international diplomacy, the Contanan Security Pact, an intergovernmental military and economic alliance of nine countries led by United Contana, has signed a five-year non-aggression pact with the Federation of Anrakan Isles. This landmark agreement underlines the CSP's commitment to broadening its influence beyond its home continent of Contana, while maintaining peaceful relations across the globe.

The pact demonstrates the CSP's ongoing efforts to peacefully extend its influence across the Anrakan Archipelago, marking an important turn in the complex geopolitical landscape. As the CSP strengthens its global position to counteract the capitalist influence of the ATO, this agreement signals a commitment to strategic, peaceful expansion that respects the sovereignty of nations that lie in the ocean between United Contana and Arcasia.
Increasing Homelessness

The region of Bergia is among the worst hit regions in Sordland where homelessness has sky-rocketed since the economic recession. The number of homeless in the city of Deyr is more likely to have increased by 25% in the last year.

The rise was particularly stark among Bludish people, where homelessness increased by 72 percent in just six years. It is reported that homelessness among ethnic minorities has reached the highest level in more than a decade. The Bludish minority of the region now account for up to 47 percent of all homeless people there.
Infrastructure Report

The recession led to a reduction in rail assets, with more than a fifth of the railway network - itself antiquated - being mothballed in the recent years. While the main lines of the railway network are currently in service, increasing demand in goods from Gelsord to the capital is pushing the network to its limits. The rail signaling system in the region dates from the middle of the last century, and is also in need of improvement.
Party Committee Report

The Reform Committee reports that any potential change to the Constitution in the direction of the reformists will likely result in strong opposition from the National Front Party. Most members of the United Sordland Party also seem reluctant about supporting such changes.

Additionally, the Chief Strategist of the President, Lucian Galade, reports that the Sollist politicians and the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court are willing to talk about a potential alliance.
Party Committee Report

The Reform Committee reports that any potential change to the Constitution that would result in the expansion of executive powers will likely result in strong opposition from the People’s Freedom and Justice Party. However, Kesaro Kibener of the National Front Party seemed to be interested in working together with the committee.

The Members of Assembly in support of such direction currently seem low, but possibly make up a huge majority in the Grand National Assembly, if the conservatives support can be taken. The reformist wing of the United Sordland Party seem reluctant about supporting such changes.
General Staff Gathers

The general staff convened right after the election to congratulate our victory. All branches of the Sordish Armed Forces were represented in the meeting that took place at Camp Strongarm with massive security measures.

The Chief of the Armed Forces Valken Kruger, made a public press statement highlighting the increasing chances of military confrontation in Eastern Merkopa and thanked us for the promise to strengthen and support the military.
GNA Prepares Tourism Act

The Grand National Assembly in Holsord is readying the Sordland Tourism and Cultural Preservation Act. This Act aims to enhance the cultural and tourism appeal of several cities, including Borin, Ribery, Lachaven, Anrica, and Benfi, in a collective push to make Sordland a global tourist destination.
Logistical Issues

In a recent update from Holsord, the Mayor expressed growing concerns about escalating traffic congestion linked to the city's burgeoning population and rapid urban expansion. A logistics report pinpointed the significant increase in traffic volume and subsequent slowing of transportation routes as the capital's most pressing issues.

The Mayor stressed that 'the lack of a comprehensively designed, large-scale, land-based logistics hub, serving as a converging point for all transporters, is exacerbating the issues faced by domestic transporters.' Given Holsord's status as a sprawling metropolis, the current situation, where transporters have established separate centers across 10 different districts, is scattered and inefficient.
Police Report on HSU Fire

A fire broke out in the academic administration building of the Holsord State University. The initial report from the chief of police in Holsord indicates a near to complete destruction of employee records from 1890 until now along with original copies of internationally recognized academic research destroyed.

The extent of the damage is worse than expected.
Public Opinion Report

People’s views on the need for democratic reform in the government’s structure has changed over the last decade. Reformist propaganda from the leader of the People’s Freedom and Justice Party, Frens Ricter, have resulted in a massive increase in the demands for democratic reforms. It is estimated that currently 55% of the population supports the reformist ideas.
Party Committee Report

The Reform Committee reports that any potential change to the Constitution in the direction of the reformists will likely result in strong opposition from the National Front Party.

The Members of Assembly in support of such direction seem to be in great numbers, and possibly make up a majority in the Grand National Assembly, while most members of the United Sordland Party seem reluctant about supporting such changes.
Security Increased

Security measures at the capital have been heightened after the murder of Bernard Circas. The mayor of Holsord reports that everything is under control.

Security around the Maroon Palace has been increased with the combined efforts of the Holsord Police Department and the Presidential Guard. Additionally, the entrance procedures to the palace are being revised with advice from security professionals.

The Police Chief Karl Greiser reported that an investigation has been launched on the murder of Bernard Circas.
SID Joins HSU Fire Investigation

Further investigations by the police department reveal a potential arson case with no identified suspects yet. The police chief of Holsord has voiced concern about suspected sabotage by a foreign nation, inviting the Sordish Intelligence Directorate in the investigation to expand the investigation.

The area is cordoned off from the public to discover further evidence.
General Staff Gathers

The general staff convened right after the election to congratulate our victory. All branches of the Sordish Armed Forces were represented in the meeting that took place at Camp Strongarm with massive security measures.

The Chief of the Armed Forces Valken Kruger, made a public press statement highlighting the increasing chances of military confrontation in Eastern Merkopa and requested support to strengthen the military.
Kyrute Expresses Approval of Sordish Democracy

The Republic of Kyrute congratulated President Anton Rayne on his recent election victory in Sordland. Chancellor Inos Adriumer of Kyrute extolled Sordland's democratic process and the peaceful transition of power, emphasizing shared values. Kyrute expressed positive outlook to continued diplomatic collaboration and mutual growth with Sordland.
Lachaven Sea Rig Maintenance

The Gasom Sea Rig off the coast of Lachaven has paused oil extraction operations for essential maintenance. The rig has been a significant contributor to Lachaven's oil output, and its temporary shutdown could impact the city's production levels. The maintenance timeline remains uncertain. The local government is monitoring the situation and making arrangements to ensure minimal disruption in the city's oil supply. 

Until then, normal operations remain suspended.
Port of Lachaven Loses Importance

The latest marine traffic reports show that the Port of Lachaven is no longer the busiest of the Merkopa continent, falling behind to the third position. While this is a negative indicator for our administration, Lachaven still has the potential to shine again as a major trading center.

The Port of Lachaven is the largest port of Sordland, and holds enormous importance for the economy, particularly as the main distribution center linking the capital and inner parts of Sordland to the rest of the world.

This major port city will hopefully keep supporting a possible economic upturn in the entire country if investment projects succeed.
Low Production In Agnland

The report calls attention to the alarmingly low levels of productivity growth in the region of Agnland, where there also are high rates of food insecurity, malnutrition, and rural poverty in inner parts of the region.
Nature Preservation March

The Nature Preservation Foundation in Leiren has organized a march promoting ecological practices and nature preservation. The event witnessed significant participation, demonstrating the local community's commitment to environmental issues. This peaceful demonstration has successfully raised awareness about Leiren's unique biodiversity and environmental challenges. 

Local authorities have noted the event and the message conveyed by the Foundation.
Infrastructure Report

The recent collapse of the tourism industry in Lenkurg has led to a reduction in trade traffic and road maintenance. The road network is currently in service but is in need of substantial improvement.

Ports, country roads, and bridges similarly suffer from a lack of investment. Firms doing business in Lenkurg report a significant shortage of warehousing facilities, particularly refrigerated facilities, with implications both for the transportation system and the ability to serve the population’s basic food and health needs.
Congratulations from Prime Minister Alvarez

Prime Minister Alvarez congratulated you for the results and spoke about his hopes to have a beneficial partnership deal in the future. He sent his best wishes to the Sordish people and warned us about the threats of the encroaching Malenyevist influence of United Contana from the east, emphasizing the importance of unity in our continent, Merkopa.
Increasing Unemployment

The number of people filing for unemployment in Morna continues to rise as the recession continues.

'The change in economic conditions is historic and stunning in its speed,' said the Mayor of Morna. 'In the aftermath of the Crisis of 1951, the unemployment rate in Morna rose to 9 percent in the following year. The last six months have almost erased all gains in employment over the last two decades.'
Gas Field Discovery

The Sordish Grid Corporation's field research team has announced new gas field discoveries in Narbel. These discoveries could enhance the city's energy supply and play a significant role in the broader energy landscape of Sordland. Preliminary analysis of the yield and quality of these fields is currently underway. The corporation will soon release a comprehensive report outlining extraction feasibility. 

The economic implications of these findings, particularly regarding potential growth and job creation in the region, are noteworthy.
Tourism Potential in Ribery

Ribery, with its rich historical sites, unique culture, and natural beauty, has untapped tourism potential. However, the city lacks the necessary infrastructure and promotional activities to become a fully-fledged tourist destination. Local officials are actively seeking further support to develop Ribery's tourism sector. Any strategic plan for Ribery's development will require a focus on infrastructure and the promotion of its attractions. 

Boosting tourism could significantly enhance the city's economy and create numerous job opportunities.
Rizia Congratulates Election Victory

King Romus Toras of Rizia has formally extended warm congratulations to President Anton Rayne following his electoral success. In an official address, he praised Sordland's so-called democratic ethos and expressed a keen interest in fortifying bilateral ties under the Rayne administration. 

The king anticipates a future of close cooperation and mutual respect between the two nations regardless of the governmental differences.
Promising Agricultural Growth

For the first time in three years the agricultural output of Sarna has increased. Many experts link the increased output to both a drop in temperatures and new farming practices that have been adopted in recent years.

Additionally, farmers are now accessing more generous credit allowances from the government that were left over from the Alphonso administration.

The Ministry of Agriculture reports that the region's agricultural industry has the potential to become a powerhouse in the future if investments persist.
Declining Energy Output at Valgen Dam

Valgen Dam, a critical energy resource for Sordland, has been experiencing a reduction in its energy output due to its age. The dam's ageing infrastructure is proving less efficient, affecting its ability to maintain previous levels of energy generation. This decrease could impact the region's energy supply if not addressed promptly. 

Plans for refurbishment or modernization of the dam could be proposed in the future if necessary.
Congratulations from Chancellor Hegel

Chancellor Hegel sent his congratulations on your great victory and wished for close cooperation between our countries in the future. Hegel signalled concessions from Valgsland in case of a promising trade deal. He also congratulated the Sordish democracy for the successful elections and warned us about the threat Arcasia’s growing influence poses for Eastern Merkopa.
Congratulations from President Smolak

President Smolak sent his congratulations on the election victory and wished for a cooperative future between Wehlen and Sordland, signalling a desire to normalise the diplomatic situation between the two countries.

Invest in Mega-Infrastructure

A decision to invest in one of two planned mega-infrastructure projects.

Invest in Arcasian Company Stocks

A personal investment opportunity has been relayed by Mr. Manger. An experienced stock broker in Ventrie City, Arcasia is selling valuable shares of Armadine Industries: an up and coming electronics manufacturing company. We could invest or let the opportunity pass.
An opportunity to buy stocks from an Arcasian company.
Alphonso Abandons Lotherberg's Exclusive Conclave

In a stunning development, former President and current Chairman of Gasom, Ewald Alphonso, has announced his departure from the exclusive Lotherberg Group. His decision has been fueled by a growing disillusionment with the interests of the secretive organization. Alphonso has been quoted saying he's intent on charting his own course, away from Lotherberg. 

However, this abrupt exit from the Group, only a few months after his defeat in the 1953 elections, marks another political setback for the man who led Sordland into its deepest recession back in 1951.
Armadine Industries Pioneering Electronics

A new prototype for the first pocket radio was displayed by the Arcasian electronics company Armadine Industries in Ventrie City. After six years of research the engineers behind the pocket transistor radio have revealed that the material science questions regarding the composites have been solved. The company is now filing the patents for the product.

The CEO of Armadine Arron Bridges is predicting an IPO at VCSE in the upcoming years. In a bid to raise further investment Mr. Bridges has called for all venture capitalists who believe in the future of science and technology in the marketplace to invest in the company.

The President of Arcasia Dwight Walker praised the bright minds of Arcasian engineers following the announcement and called for further technological advancements for the military industrial complex.
Restructure the Infrastructure?

After the recent successful mega-infrastructure projects from United Contana and Valgsland the world is warming up to the idea as a source of growth and employment. But is there any truth to this success?

Our investment analysis indicates that infrastructure investments can be fruitful in the short-term but even more so in the long-term especially if they focus on linking economic nodes that business logistics depend on. This is however the first step, the crux of the matter is diversification of investment where the government supports employment and growth. It is key to help private businesses with government contracts, tax breaks and political support in order to create a self-sufficient and dynamic economy.

The government's role in Sordland should be to integrate to the world economy and reap the benefits of global trade. Economic growth and income inequality in this country won't be fixed otherwise.
End Sollonomics!

A new era begins for Sordland and it holds many economic questions that will need to be answered by President Rayne.

Our top economic analysts with consultation from the National Business Council have released a comprehensive report on the performance of the past twenty years. A certain section of the report stands out: the last two four-year plans of the planned doctrine created a budget deficit and a clear reduction of the industrial production output. This was specifically due to mismanagement and inefficient bureaucracy.

The year on year growth, budget balance and production index values indicate that the two most productive consecutive years had been when the privatization programme of Alphonso began in 1949. Our editorial team with the help of experts like Mikail Aven and Edith Agnoc have come to the conclusion that the recession was not actually caused by Alphonsonomics but by the drastic obstructions of state executives hindering the plan.

President Rayne must take the advice of planned economy proponents around him with a pinch of salt, otherwise he could find himself in the same spot of Tarquin Soll in the mid 40’s.
Sordland's Regional Trade

As the Rayne administration starts its first term, there is a question in all of our heads. What will be the regional international trade policy?

Due to the strategic geopolitical location of Sordland, historically Agnolia and Wehlen have been natural trading partners. Depending on the direction of the Rayne administration, we think it is likely that a new trade deal will be brokered with at least one of these partners in the near term.

All in all, regardless of which trading partners the administration decides to go with, one thing is for sure. Regional trade will boost the ailing economy.

The real question is what does Valgsland or Lespia think about Sordland?
Rizia Firmly Refutes Pales' Retort in Aureus Gas Fields Dispute

In a recent twist to the Aureus offshore gas fields saga, the Kingdom of Rizia has strongly refuted the Grand Duchy of Pales' counterclaim. This development escalates last year's surprise move by Rizia, which asserted ownership based on historical records and longstanding ANDOR maritime agreements. The claim had initially put significant pressure on Pales and caused notable fluctuations in Merkopan energy markets.

The Grand Duchy of Pales, countering Rizia's assertions, had presented their own historical evidence and legal agreements to justify their exploitation rights. This counterclaim added fuel to the already intense dispute, drawing keen attention from across Merkopa and prompting offers of international mediation to prevent further escalation.

Despite the ongoing diplomatic efforts, the deadlock continues to unsettle the region's energy sector. Energy companies across Merkopa express growing concerns about operational disruptions and potential impacts on the region's energy supply. The persistence of this dispute threatens not only immediate economic interests but also the long-term stability of energy markets.
President Vetoes Bill

The Campaign Finance Bill has been vetoed by President Rayne after its approval from the Grand National Assembly by majority vote on Friday following a three-hour debate.

Frens Ricter - who also objected to the funding package saying it contained too much unfairness in the allocation of the budget - also sought to delay proceedings by demanding a formal recorded vote, but was overruled. The bill passed the Assembly, but failed to become law by President Rayne’s decision.
Campaign Bill: Fair Representation in the Assembly

The long-stalled Campaign Bill has once again taken centre stage in the Grand National Assembly. The bill, first proposed during the Alphonso Presidency, had been put on hold due to the 1953 election but has now been resurrected under President Anton Rayne. The proposed amendments ensure a more proportional allocation of public funds, more accurately reflecting a party's influence within the legislative body.
A Committee For Reforms

Speaker Gloria Tory said that a committee which includes all three political parties of the Assembly, has been formed for the preparation of potential changes to the constitution. The committee has been asked to submit a comprehensive report to find a solution for the current problematic state of affairs in the governmental institutions.

Tory said, 'USP wants to appeal to the people of Sordland to help in maintaining stability and order in the state.' The details of the committee regarding its actual topics or its members have not been clarified.
Electoral Funding Reform

The Campaign Finance Bill has been signed into law by President Rayne after the approval of the Grand National Assembly by majority vote on Friday following a three-hour debate.

Frens Ricter - who objected to the funding package saying it contained too much unfairness in the allocation of the budget - also sought to delay proceedings by demanding a formal recorded vote, but was overruled.

The new law brings small changes to the criteria for the allocation of the campaign budgets, and introduces no changes to the total amount of public funds reserved for the political parties which stands as 100 million SR.
Fire Strikes Holsord State University Archive

A sudden fire broke out in the archives of the Holsord State University engulfing a significant part of the academic administration building. It was put out by the local firefighters after burning for 8 hours and ravaging through the historic library which housed many priceless documents.

Reporters on the scene have relayed that the event occurred in the evening with multiple staff of the faculty being transported to the hospital with severe burns but no deaths occurred. The rector Sander Navek immediately commented that the incident has damaged several academic works and employee records. “We might have lost the world or we might have lost Merkopa. We won't know until the day when we can enter the facility to evaluate.”.
Rayne Spoke of Change and Hope

President Anton Rayne has been sworn into duty in a great ceremony in Holsord. Thousands have attended the ceremony where President Rayne has met with his supporters for the first time after his election.

In his inauguration, Rayne spoke about change and hope, bringing focus on reforms. 'Together, we will bring prosperity and reform to our nation. It is a time of hope, it is a time of change,' said the new President before he went on to start his first day in the Maroon Palace.
Rayne Emphasized Sordland’s Dire Situation

President Anton Rayne has been sworn into duty in a great ceremony in Holsord. Thousands have attended the ceremony where President Rayne has met with his supporters for the first time after his election.

In his inauguration, Rayne spoke about the current dire situation, bringing focus on the suffering of Sordish people. 'We are enduring economic hardship like never before, and today, our nation is falling apart,' said the new President before he went on to start his first day in the Maroon Palace.
Rayne Spoke of Unity

President Anton Rayne has been sworn into duty in a great ceremony in Holsord. Thousands have attended the ceremony where President Rayne has met with his supporters for the first time after his election.

In his inauguration, Rayne spoke of unity, bringing focus on 'people’s right for a free and prosperous life.' 'For many generations, this country and its long history have kept us tied to an idea, the idea of unity' said the new President before he went on to start his first day in the Maroon Palace.
Tourism: A Beacon of Hope for Sordland

The Sordland Tourism and Cultural Preservation Act, currently under deliberation in the Grand National Assembly, is a shining beacon of hope. Aimed at enhancing the tourism appeal of Borin, Ribery, Lachaven, Anrica, and Benfi, the Act promises to position Sordland as a global tourist destination. 

As the nation grapples with economic hardship, the bill's potential to boost tourism and cultural preservation efforts provides a much-needed silver lining.
Support in Assembly Grows For Campaign Finance Bill

A bill to change the criteria for the allocation of public funds to political parties is proposed by Representative Albin Clavin from the USP. The bill aims to change the criteria from the proportion of votes won in general elections to proportion of seats won by a political party in the Grand National Assembly. This would result in an increase of about 28 million SR to the governing United Sordland Party which will benefit the most from the proposed bill.

The new bill would give political parties an annual amount of 500.000 SR per Member of Assembly.
Freezing Temperatures Recorded

The Meteorological Institute has reported the record low temperature of minus 29 in the city of Uziren. A warning for frostbite has been issued in the cities of southern Bergia. People are advised not to go out unless they must due to the risk of frostbite. Schools are closed for this period.
Gasom Hires Freeze Amid Economic Strains

As Sordland grapples with economic challenges, Gasom, one of the nation's largest corporations, has announced a freeze on new hires. The corporation, integral to Sordland's energy sector and a significant contributor to its economy, has yet to announce when it intends to lift the hiring freeze. While this development is a blow to the Sordish workforce, it's a reminder of the delicate state of our nation's economy.
Murder at the Palace!

Breaking News! Bernard Circas, a prominent independent MP known for his communist romanticism has been murdered leaving the Maroon Palace grounds after the inauguration ball of Anton Rayne.

Reports indicate a politically motivated assault by the far-right nationalists of the Young Sords. Shocking photographs have been leaked to the press showing blood dripped stairs of the Maroon Palace. We heavily condemn this sort of political violence, this is the very cycle the President must break with reforms.
SORDISH NATIONAL LEAGUE STARTS SEASON

As the Sordish National League prepares to kick off its 1954-1955 season, the excitement and anticipation surrounding the league is greater than ever before. Football, once a minor pastime in Sordland, has steadily grown in popularity over the past decade, with the National League emerging as the premier platform for the country's top teams to showcase their skills and compete for the coveted championship title.

FC Gelsord, last season's champions, return with a core of experienced veterans, including star striker Hakon Brenner, who holds the top-scorer title of the league since 1952.

Meanwhile, FC Anrica have managed to add several new players to their lineup after new investments coming to the club, and is looking to bounce back after disappointing seasons and reclaim their spots as contenders for the championship.

While it's impossible to predict whether FC Gelsord will finally be bested this season, one thing is certain: the Sordish National League is slowly cementing itself as a force in the world of football, and the 1954-1955 season is sure to be a testament to the league's growing prestige and popularity.
The New Assembly Begins Duty

President Anton Rayne has been elected 4th President of Sordland in the 7th Sordish elections. The United Sordland Party has won the election on Sunday with just over 37 percent of the vote, while Frens Ricter, the leader of the People’s Freedom and Justice Party, could gain just over 20 percent.

Kesaro Kibener, the head of the right-wing National Front Party, is in third place with just over 11 percent.

The Communist Party of Sordland and the Workers Party of Bludia both won just below 10 percent of the vote, failing to pass the 10 percent election threshold.

The new term begins with the opposition of PFJP and NFP under the USP government. The unrepresented votes below the threshold resulted in the USP taking 52 percent of the seats in the Grand National Assembly, giving them the lawmaking power. The new seat numbers have been finalized as follows: USP 130, PFJP 70, NFP 40 and Independents 10.
Alphonso Ditches Lotherberg: A Sign of Discord

Ewald Alphonso, the once influential political figure and former President, has publicly severed ties with the influential Lotherberg Group. Frustrated by the Group's direction, Alphonso, the current Chairman of Gasom, is determined to steer his own path. Despite this apparent show of independence, one can't help but view his decision as a demonstration of a growing rift within Lotherberg. 

Alphonso's political failures including a devastating loss to President Anton Rayne in the 1953 elections and his triggering of the 1951 recession, cast a long shadow over this move.
Another USP President

How many times will people fall for the same trap? We’ve seen this before with Colonel Soll, who supposedly saved this country and brought stability in times of chaos. His stability, however, meant a life of oppression. Any opposing voices were silenced and many were persecuted. Next was Alphonso, who was elected as the liberal reformer to bring change to the USP and Sordland. Seeing his unfortunate inability, his own cabinet resigned.

As the third USP candidate becomes president, it is high time to realise that real change won't come from their party.
Unfair Campaign Finance Bill Crushed

A new bill that further expands on the unfairness of our election system has been approved by the Grand National Assembly and was later vetoed by President Rayne. Rayne deserves credit for crushing the undemocratic proposal, even though it came from his own party and would have benefitted himself.

The bill sought to change the rules of eligibility of the public funds that are reserved for every political party in Sordland. It eliminates every party from eligibility to the funds, apart from the three that are currently in the Assembly.

The insane proposal would have also resulted in the governing United Sordland Party’s share from the funds to double. Luckily, President Rayne showed us that he can go against his own party when it needs to be done.
Glamorous Inaugural Ball

The Holsord elite gathers for a lavish state ball. Many citizens in the country are uncertain about their own future but the state has no problems with wasting taxpayer's money right from the start.

We demand that these traditions of wasteful nature will become a thing of the past once the President settles in. The team here at the Radical will keep fighting for a better, more equal tomorrow for all.
USP Hijacks Elections

A new law that further expands on the unfairness of our election system has been approved by the Grand National Assembly and was signed into law by President Rayne.

The new law changes the rules of eligibility of the public funds that are reserved for every political party in Sordland. Previously, the funds were given on the basis of the number of votes in the general elections. With these changes, the funds will be given on the basis of the number of seats the political party holds, which eliminates every party apart from the three that are currently in the Assembly.

This insane law also results in the governing United Sordland Party’s share from the funds to double. As Anton Rayne’s presidency begins, we at The Radical, are already smelling the rot in Holsord.
Nationalist Violence
